title: Find Words Containing Character
statement: You get an array of strings `words` and one lowercase letter `x`. Collect every index `i` for which the string `words[i]` has `x` somewhere in it (at least once), and return those indices. The indices may come back in any order; if no word has `x`, return an empty array.
constraints: x is a lowercase English letter
Every words[i] contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Each word is judged on its own: either the letter `x` appears in it or it does not. So the task is a plain scan of every word's characters, recording the word's index the first time `x` turns up. With at most 50 words of 50 letters, even checking every character is tiny.

## Approach

1. Start an empty list `result`.
2. For each index `i`, take `word = words[i]`.
3. Walk the characters `ch` of `word`. As soon as one equals `x`, push `i` into `result` and `break`, so the index is added only once.
4. After all words are scanned, return `result` (its indices are in increasing order, which is one of the accepted orders).

## Example 1, step by step

`words = ["leet", "code"]`, `x = "e"`.

- `i = 0`, `word = "leet"`: `"l"` differs, `"e"` matches, so push `0` and stop scanning this word.
- `i = 1`, `word = "code"`: `"c"`, `"o"`, `"d"` differ, `"e"` matches, so push `1`.

The answer is `[0, 1]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(L), where L is the total number of characters, since each character is looked at at most once.
- Space: O(n) for the returned indices; the scan itself uses O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Forgetting the `break` pushes the same index once per occurrence, so `"leet"` would add `0` twice.
- Return word indices, not the positions of `x` inside a word.
- When no word matches, return an empty array, not `null` or `-1`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `result` | indices of the words that contain `x` |
| `i` | index of the current word |
| `word` | the current word, `words[i]` |
| `ch` | the current character inside `word` |

narration.2: Prepare an empty list for the indices of matching words.
narration.3: Visit the words one by one by index.
narration.4: Take the current word so its letters can be scanned.

narration.6: Is this character the letter we are looking for?
narration.7: Yes: this word contains x, so record its index.
narration.8: One match is enough; stop scanning this word so the index is not added twice.
